judge: Two judges, each a Claude agent shown only the match sheet's claims and truth, not which method made the claims, ruled on every claim without seeing each other's rulings. An adjudicating agent ruled on each claim where they differed. Rules: the same problem at the same place; a general claim states nothing; when unsure, no match.

Sheet index on G0.1 lists A7.1 but the set has no such sheet.
A1.1 title block reads SECOND FLOOR PLAN while the drawing label reads FIRST FLOOR PLAN.

Building-wide single-exit claim on G1.2 names neither the third nor the fourth floor in words or by sheet (rule 4 requires naming each), and the third floor's actual deficiency is a stair left off entirely; declined under rules 2 and 9.

Adjudicated: The claim and exit_capacity point at the same Stair 1 marker on G1.2. The claim's 15-in width gives exactly 50 occupants at the standard stair factor of 0.3 in per occupant (15/0.3 = 50), which is the truth item's figure. The 45 in the claim cites from G0.1, G1.3 and G1.4 would give 150, which is above the load of 71, so the 15 in is the changed value behind the 50-person capacity. A width below the minimum and a capacity below the load are the same undersized-stair defect in different units. Rule 1 allows any wording, and rule 6 accepts a claim that describes the visible symptom. The 0.3 factor is standard code knowledge, not content from another file, and the numbers fit exactly, so there is no factual doubt for rule 9. The second judge's ruling stands.
